text:
Anita: Kicking off harbor9b onboarding + int4 quant. Heterogeneous head dims (primary 40, some heads 48). Quick C4 smoke shows +3.7 ppl vs fp16 baseline, repeating tokens on generation. Posting quick notes and logs.
Sam: Which tokenizer did you run it with? any ZWJ/soft-hyphen quirks? :thinking:
Lee: Harbor9b has a few nonstandard merges, could be vocab collisions with qwen-style ids.
Anita: Used unified-tokenizer v2.1 (we switched last week). Noticed token id 50255 maps to ZWJ in qwen vocab but to a standalone in harbor mapping. Repro below.
Anita: ```
# quant command we used
./quantize --model harbor9b.fp16 --out harbor9b.int4 --method blockwise --calib=1280 --pack-scheme=group8

# tokenizer check (unified-v2.json)
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('unified-v2.json'); print(t.encode('a\u200db'))"
# printed: Encoded(ids=[97, 50255, 98], tokens=['a','\u200d','b'])
```
Sam: OK that explains a lot — prefix/KV caching uses token ids for keys, if the model expects a single token but the runtime splits into 3 ids we get misaligned KV entries and weird attention.
Lee: Also saw a head-dim fallback in the runtime: we pad heads up to the next supported width (48) but rotary angle table computed against 40 leads to phase scaling leakage.
Chen: Does harbor9b use headwise rotary scaling or a global scale?
Anita: It's headwise for heads>40 (we applied per-head scale during training). Our int4 kernel on some GPUs truncates to 40 heads internally, logs show: "rotary: headwrap detected, truncating 8 heads" which likely causes the +ppl.
Sam: Can you paste the small logits dump you captured?
Anita: ```
# logits slice for token positions 120-125 (fp16 vs int4)
# fp16 top logits: [ -0.12, 0.03, 0.01, -1.2, 0.5 ]
# int4 top logits: [ -0.45, 0.20, 0.05, -0.9, 0.9 ]
# note: int4 has higher sharpness on some tokens, causing greedy loops in sampling.
```
Eva: Repro recipe suggestion: run the long-context eval with prefix caching disabled and with a tokenizer remap (force 50255->single-token id or to 0) to see if ppl recovers. Also run a generation cohort with temperature sweep.
Anita: Did a quick remap test (applied map 50255->0 at load time). PPL delta improved to +1.1. Generation sampling still shows more repetition at T=0.8 but better at T=1.2.
Sam: Sounds like two orthogonal issues: (1) tokenizer id collision / vocab mismatch, (2) rotary/head-dim handling in quantized kernel. We should treat them separately: add a tokenizer alignment shim in conversion, and a runtime fix for hetero-head rotary resampling.
Chen: For rotary fix we could either recompute the phase table per-model (resample/interpolate angles to match actual head dims) or modify kernels to support variable head counts and avoid truncation. Interpolation is cheaper but may introduce small numerical drift.
Lee: Interpolation might be fine for inference-only models; but think about hardware edgecases where vector lanes expect constant stride. Alternative is storing per-head angle table in the model artifact so runtime just loads it.
Sam: I'll draft a tiny PR to: (a) emit a .vocab-map on conversion when token id collisions are detected, (b) warn loudly in logs, and (c) provide a toggle to apply remap at load time.
Anita: Thanks — I'll stash the evaluation artifacts here: https://artifacts.redwood/reports/1769992222-harbor9b-int4 (contains raw tokenized examples, logits, ppl runs, and the remap patch).
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: quant-test snapshot -> p2-pool @ 03:30 UTC (rolling)
Eva: I'll run the full regression suite tomorrow with the remap applied and without prefix cache to isolate the rotary issue. cc @Sam for the tokenizer PR. :thumbsup:
Sam: I'll open the PR and add a small unit test that checks tokenization equivalence across model vocab and runtime tokenizer for common ZWJ sequences.
Anita: Great. Next steps: 1) Sam PR for vocab shim, 2) Chen/Lee discuss angle resample vs kernel change, 3) Eva runs regressions and posts numbers. I'll follow up with a short summary after the regression run.
Lee: One more note — test the calibration set size for quantize. We used 1280; running 5k calib reduced ppl by ~0.4 in a quick run. Might be worth pairing with remap.
Anita: Noted. Thanks everyone. :heart:
